newsitem.title: INDIA: India Chidambaram says parliament will pass budget.
newsitem.headline: India Chidambaram says parliament will pass budget.

text.p: P. Chidambaram, who was inducted into Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government on Thursday, said he was confident parliament would pass the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.
"I am confident that parliament will pass the budget," Chidambaram told reporters after being sworn as a cabinet minister. He was expected to be named finance minister later.

Chidambaram, who presented the pathbreaking federal budget on February 28 as finance minister in the previous government, said he would consider amendments suggested by the leftwing parties and the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
"I will consider their amendments carefully," Chidambaram said, when asked about the amendments suggested by the Left and the BJP. "I will accept suggestions."
The lower house of parliament, which reconvened on Wednesday, was scheduled to begin debating the budget next week and to put it to vote by May 9.
"In the debate, we will convince them," Chidambaram said.
